annotation.title_clean: Possible outcome of 2019 Group of Governmental Experts and future actions of international community on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
annotation.title_en: Possible outcome of 2019 Group of Governmental Experts and future actions of international community on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Government of Japan (submitted to CCW GGE on LAWS)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS (CCW/GGE.1/2019/WP.3)
annotation.summary_en: Japan's working paper to the CCW GGE on LAWS argues rules should target lethal, fully autonomous weapons lacking meaningful human control, without restricting civilian autonomous-technology R&D. It stresses IHL compliance and State/individual responsibility, proposes Article 36 weapons-review reporting for confidence building, and favours a political outcome document over a binding instrument.
key_provisions_or_claims: Scope of rules should be limited to lethal, fully autonomous weapons without meaningful human control
Meaningful human control is indispensable and underpins responsibility attribution
R&D on autonomous technologies should not be restricted merely due to potential diversion to weapons
IHL violations by autonomous systems attributable to States or individuals
Binding instrument premature; propose outcome document and Article 36 reporting via CCW annual reports
